test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 11 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

I’m sorry I snapped at you earlier, I think I (am just in a bad mood today).

options.text: got up on the wrong side of the bed

solution:
The correct answer is "**got up on the wrong side of the bed.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Idiom is an expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of the individual words in it.
 
 
• Example: To "bite off more than you can chew" is an idiom that means you have tried to do something which is too difficult for you.
 
 
 
• **Now in the given sentence, the phrase "I am just in a bad mood today" can be replaced by the idiom in option 4.**
 
• **The idiom "got up on the wrong side of the bed" means to be in a bad mood or to start the day off badly.**
 
• The phrase is often used to explain someone's grumpiness or irritability.
 
 
• Example: Try not to wake up on the wrong side of the bed tomorrow. You’re awfully grouchy today!
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In option 1, "two wrongs don't make right," means that it is not justified to respond to a wrong action with another wrong action.
 
• In option 2, "clam up," means to become silent or refuse to speak.
 
• In option 3, "dressed to the nines," means to be dressed very elegantly or extravagantly.
